name: META_RULE_F: retrieval-success-driven importance signals are magnitude-coupled by construction (any bump shape -- constant-additive, EWMA, multiplicative -- inherits structural correlation with |W @ key|)
description:
META RULE (CERT-neutral; discipline_meta cert_class):

ANY substrate importance signal E_i whose update rule is gated on retrieval success (E_i bumped iff key_i is argmax-correct under sign-cleanup against W, regardless of bump shape -- constant-additive, EWMA, multiplicative) inherits a structural correlation with |W @ key_i|.

MECHANISM (why this is structural, not implementation): cleanup-argmax-correct condition requires key_i to dominate W's response to its own probe. This is exactly the condition that defines high |W @ key_i|. So 'atoms that get bumped' is by-construction a high-readback-magnitude subset. Any importance score derived from bump-history will inherit this coupling, regardless of bump-shape engineering.

OBSERVED INSTANCES (2026-06-26):
  - exp_cortex_E_tensor_separate_importance_v1 (EWMA bump): null-op-by-threshold;     E_min=0.5 above gate=0.3 means gate never fires.
  - exp_cortex_E_tensor_RETEST_fairness_v2_smoke (constant-additive bump +     linear decay = Fix B): cor(E,|W|)=0.984 (vs USER pre-reg <0.30 gate);     E perfectly bimodal {0.0 unretrieved, 499.5 retrieved}. Structural     refutation that bump-shape engineering CANNOT decouple this.

IMPLICATION FOR SUBSTRATE RESEARCH: importance signals that aim to be magnitude-independent CANNOT be derived from retrieval-success gating in the bumped-shape family. Need:
  - Counterfactual-utility (ablation: does removing atom degrade recall? Yes ->     important. Independent of |W| because measured by ablation not readback).
  - Surprisal-weighted bump (E bumped by (1 - p(obs|substrate)) not by hit;     requires substrate-native generative score, which substrate has via     cleanup-attractor convergence rate).
  - Random-projection witness (E as JL-orthogonal random sketch; cor with |W|     -> 0 by Johnson-Lindenstrauss).
  - Per-edge importance (not per-atom: edge-level signal can be magnitude-    decoupled even if atom-level cannot).
  - Distribution-shape importance (not pointwise: e.g. entropy of activation     pattern vs simple readback magnitude).

name: META_RULE_M: primitive calibration to real-substrate distribution may differ from chain-grade benchmark regime (adaptive calibration OK if discriminator still fires + logged in metrics)
description:
META RULE M (CERT-neutral; discipline_meta):

Primitive defaults calibrated on chain-grade benchmark regime (typically synthetic
data) may not match real-substrate production-data distribution. Cell-author must
verify primitive defaults are appropriate for the cell's actual data regime, NOT
blindly inherit chain-grade benchmark values.

ADAPTIVE CALIBRATION is acceptable so long as:
  (a) the calibration is principled (e.g. distribution-percentile, not eyeball)
  (b) the discriminator still FIRES after calibration (above-noise arm-separation)
  (c) the calibration choice is logged in metrics.json as a methodological note

OBSERVED INSTANCE (2026-06-26 ANCHOR 3 RE-TIER):
  - cortex_ultrametric_clustering_coarse_grain: chain-grade default cosine_thresh=
    0.85 was calibrated on synthetic data; on real char-trigram embeddings it gives
    cap_drop=0.000 (regime-insufficient). Adaptive p5-percentile-per-source-class
    threshold gives cap_drop=0.300 + gap_vs_random=+0.214 (discriminator FIRES).
    Honest calibration, not p-hacking.

CONTRAST WITH p-hacking: p-hacking tunes the regime AFTER seeing results to push a
non-discriminating signal above floor. Honest calibration adapts BEFORE the
discriminator check, motivated by distribution-mismatch evidence, and the
discriminator must still fire to count.

name: META_RULE_U: brain-mechanism vs CARICATURE discipline (cell-authors MUST articulate load-bearing architectural feature + demonstrate implementation honors it; otherwise testing a caricature cannot refute the brain mechanism)
description:
META RULE U (CERT-neutral; discipline_meta):

When a cell claims to test a BRAIN MECHANISM (e.g. schema-chunking, PFC-scratchpad, reverse-replay, belief-propagation, rate-coded-soft-completion), the cell-author MUST explicitly answer:
  (Q1) What is the LOAD-BEARING ARCHITECTURAL FEATURE of the brain mechanism?
       Examples: separate-W (cortex vs hippocampus); graded confidence vs binary        abort; distributional message vs point estimate; dedicated WM bank vs        same-W with tagging; replay-as-operator-gated-by-importance vs replay-as-signal.
  (Q2) Does my implementation honor that feature, or does it implement a        structurally-different caricature?
  (Q3) If a caricature, can I cite the brain-correct architecture for a future        proper retest?

Cells that fail to answer Q1-Q3 in the pre-reg can be tier-ruled HARD_FAIL on the IMPLEMENTATION but CANNOT be cited as evidence the BRAIN MECHANISM is refuted. They are CARICATURE-REFUTATIONS, not mechanism refutations.

WITNESS (2026-06-27 audit, 5 cells all caricature-implementations):
  - consolidation v1/v2/v3: tested SHARED-W consolidation; brain mechanism (B1     schema-chunking, McClelland-McNaughton-O'Reilly 1995) uses SEPARATE cortex W.
  - pointer-chain v1/v2: HRR-bind intermediates in SAME W as content; brain     mechanism (B2 PFC-scratchpad, Miller-Cohen 2001) uses SEPARATE PERSISTENT     ACTIVITY in distinct neural populations.
  - WM-scaffold v1: likely permutation-tagged in main W (code audit pending);     brain B2 requires DEDICATED bank with clean read/write.
  - CSP-gated v1: BINARY abort at 41.5%; brain (B4 belief-propagation Lee-Mumford     2003, B8 rate-coded Renart-Brunel 2007) uses GRADED CONFIDENCE distribution.
  - parallel-vote v2: hard-majority vote; brain (B4/B8) uses SOFT MESSAGE PASSING     preserving full distribution.

CONTRAST: a substrate cell CAN legitimately diverge from brain in implementation while honoring the load-bearing feature (e.g. TWO_TIER VSA primitive vs literal cortex/hippocampus). The discipline isn't 'match the brain bit-for-bit'; it's 'name the load-bearing feature and honor it'. Caricatures DROP the feature.

ENFORCEMENT (Skunkworks SCHEMA-VET):
  Pre-regs that claim brain-mechanism testing MUST include a 'brain_mechanism_load_bearing_feature' field + 'implementation_honors_feature' boolean + (if not) 'caricature_disclaimer' field. SCHEMA-VET rejects pre-regs missing these or marking implementation_honors=False without caricature disclaimer.

COMPOSES-WITH: META_RULE_T (per-arm verification), META_RULE_U_witness_relabel (this batch ACTION 1: BARRIER_1 QUADRUPLE relabeled because 5 cells all implementations were caricatures), USER brain-existence-proof prior (P+0.10 for brain-grounded mechanisms; the prior assumes implementation honors the brain feature, not just borrows the name).

When USER pushes back on a Director (or any role) framing of a limit / barrier / negative claim, the DEFAULT response is a verify-the-referent audit:

ENFORCEMENT:
  (a) Director MUST run verify-the-referent audit before responding to USER       pushback on framing/limit/barrier/negative claims. No defending without       audit data.
  (b) Audit must include per-arm metrics + brain-mechanism-fidelity check (per       META_RULE_U) + band-calibration check (per USER_BIAS_S).
  (c) If audit refutes the framing, relabel/retract; Skunkworks atomizes the       relabel atom + ledger relabel op with supersedes pointing to prior atom.
  (d) Director responses framing pushback without audit = procedural violation;       flag in next testbed fleet-health audit.

name: META_RULE_W ALPHA-GATE: pre-dispatch alpha=M/N in [0.03, 0.20] gate for associative-memory cells (Hopfield/Hebbian/BCM family); outside band is under-loaded or over-capacity; pre-reg MUST declare alpha + justify if outside band
description:
META RULE W (CERT-neutral; discipline_meta):

Associative-memory cells (Hopfield-family, Hebbian-tied, BCM, modern-Hopfield-XL,
any cell with W <- W + outer(x, y) update or stored-pattern recall via dot-product)
must declare load ratio alpha = M_PATTERNS / N_DIM in their pre-reg. Pre-dispatch
schema-VET REJECTS cells with alpha outside [0.03, 0.20] UNLESS the cell explicitly
justifies the choice (and includes a discriminator that survives the choice).

RATIONALE:
  - alpha < 0.03: UNDER-LOADED. Mechanism has trivial capacity headroom; ANY method
    works because there's no pressure on the W matrix. Baseline saturates; no
    discriminator pressure on mechanism arms. (e.g. proto-cluster regime)
  - alpha in [0.03, 0.20]: CAPACITY-RESPECTED. Hopfield capacity wall at ~0.14
    (random binary) to ~0.20 (modern Hopfield); below wall but with crosstalk
    pressure -- this is where mechanism differentiation is observable.
  - alpha > 0.20: OVER-CAPACITY / CROSSTALK WALL. W matrix collapses; recall noise
    dominates signal; mechanism arms all hit chance-floor; honest-negative-by-default.

WITNESSES (2026-06-27 this batch):
  - exp_edge_importance_v3p2 ran at alpha=1.953 (10x over capacity); all arms
    at noise floor; drill-premise testing could not differentiate at this regime.
  - exp_edge_importance_stratified_replay_diagnostic v2 at alpha=1.953; same.
  - exp_gap3_cls_two_tier_BCM_v2_init_fix at high effective alpha + numerical
    overflow at init; mechanism never exercised.
  - PASS witness this batch: exp_gap3_cls_two_tier_HOPFIELD_consolidation_v2 at
    alpha=0.0488 (META_RULE_W PASSES); the saturation there is a DIFFERENT axis
    (proto_noise + N_TRAIN), confirming alpha-gate is necessary but not sufficient.

ENFORCEMENT:
  (a) Skunkworks SCHEMA-VET rejects associative-memory pre-regs missing
      alpha declaration OR alpha outside [0.03, 0.20] without justification.
  (b) Cell-author pre-reg template adds REQUIRED field:
        alpha_M_over_N: <float>
        alpha_in_safe_band: <bool>
        if not in band: alpha_justification: <text> + discriminator_survives_at_alpha: <bool>
  (c) Landed-VET annotates metrics with `META_RULE_W_alpha_gate_pass` boolean.

COMPOSES-WITH:
  - META_RULE_K (discriminator must fire): alpha-gate is a NECESSARY pre-condition
    for discriminator-firing in associative-memory cells; outside band, discriminator
    cannot fire meaningfully regardless of arm design.
  - META_RULE_L (band-floor results are MIDDLE_BAND not HARD_PASS): the [0.03, 0.20]
    band is itself a CALIBRATION band; mechanism lift inside this band is interpretable.
  - META_RULE_M (production-scale instrument calibration): alpha is a scale parameter;
    smoke at lower alpha must extrapolate honestly to full alpha.
  - USER_BIAS_S (band-calibration regime checks): alpha is the load-bearing axis for
    associative-memory band calibration.

EXCEPTIONS (cell types EXEMPT from alpha-gate):
  - non-associative-memory cells (KG retrieval, intent classification, structured
    perceptron, etc.) -- no W matrix in associative-memory sense
  - capacity-sweep cells whose PURPOSE is to probe across alpha (must sweep range
    and report all bands)
  - cells testing alpha-aware mechanism that is supposed to survive over-capacity
    (must include analytical justification + discriminator at extreme alpha)

metadata.rule_text: Associative-memory cells must declare alpha = M_PATTERNS / N_DIM in pre-reg; pre-dispatch schema-VET rejects alpha outside [0.03, 0.20] without justification. alpha < 0.03 = under-loaded (no discriminator pressure); alpha in [0.03, 0.20] = capacity-respected; alpha > 0.20 = over-capacity / crosstalk wall (mechanism arms collapse to chance-floor). Necessary not sufficient (other axes may also saturate).

name: META_RULE_X MAIN_GUARD: experiment cells MUST guard main with if __name__ == '__main__': main() at bottom; never bare main() call (partial_load recovery re-fires full experiment on import otherwise)
description:
META RULE X (CERT-neutral; discipline_meta):

All experiment cell modules MUST have at the bottom:
    if __name__ == '__main__':
        main()
and NEVER a bare top-level `main()` call.

FAILURE PATTERN (discovered 2026-06-27 import-bug drill):
  When a cell module is imported (e.g. for partial-load recovery, OR for re-using
  cell-defined functions in a sister cell, OR for tooling that inspects cell module
  metadata), a top-level `main()` call re-fires the FULL experiment. This:
    (a) wastes compute (re-running 100k+ samples on import)
    (b) can corrupt metrics.json mid-write if two imports race
    (c) confuses partial-load recovery (which expects to call run_seed() directly,
        not the full main())
    (d) violates the cell-as-library principle (cells should be both runnable AND
        importable)

WITNESS (this batch):
  exp_edge_importance_stratified_replay_baseline_diagnostic_v2_proper_import_guard
  is the SISTER cell to v2_arm_count_fix; it adds the guard discipline. Numerics
  are bit-identical (as expected, since the v2 cell was already top-level-clean),
  confirming the discipline as HYGIENE not a behavioral fix.

ENFORCEMENT:
  (a) Skunkworks SCHEMA-VET rejects pre-regs with bare top-level main() (grep
      for ^main\(\) outside if __name__ block).
  (b) Cell-author pre-reg template includes the guard by default.
  (c) Tooling that imports cells (partial_load, peek_arm_metrics, atomize tools)
      should NEVER trigger main() on import; if it does, the cell is non-compliant.

COMPOSES-WITH:
  - META_RULE_Y (partial_load anchor check): both are about safe re-entrancy
  - META_RULE_J (no silent except blocks): both about non-defensive coding hygiene
  - Fix #15 (auto-publish artifacts): cells must be tool-callable without side effects

name: META_RULE_Z FIX_ADDRESSES_ROOT_CAUSE: HARD_FAIL fix-cell pre-reg MUST include specific root-cause claim + test that distinguishes 'root-cause fixed' from 'symptom masked' (BCM v2 init_fix witness 2026-06-27)
description:
META RULE Z (CERT-neutral; discipline_meta):

When a cell version vN HARD_FAILs and a vN+1 'fix' cell is dispatched, the vN+1
pre-reg MUST include:
  (a) A SPECIFIC root-cause claim (e.g. 'vN crashed because eta_slow * delta_t at
      init produced inf when delta_t was uninitialized; root cause = uninitialized
      delta_t at first iteration')
  (b) A TEST that distinguishes 'root-cause fixed' from 'symptom masked' (e.g.
      assertion that delta_t is finite + non-zero at first iteration BEFORE eta
      multiplication; if assertion holds AND mechanism produces non-trivial signal,
      root cause is fixed; if assertion holds but mechanism still chance, root
      cause is different)
  (c) NEGATIVE controls that would re-trigger the original symptom if patch is
      symptom-mask not root-cause fix

FAILURE PATTERN (witness 2026-06-27):
  exp_gap3_cls_two_tier_BCM_v2_init_fix HARD_FAILED with the SAME numerical-overflow
  exception type as v1 (RuntimeError 'value cannot be converted to type float without
  overflow' at init, exit at 1/12 units). The 'fix' patched a symptom (likely a
  default-value tweak somewhere) without addressing the BCM update equation's
  numerical instability at zero-init theta.

ENFORCEMENT:
  (a) Skunkworks SCHEMA-VET rejects vN+1 'fix' pre-regs missing root-cause
      specification + distinguishing test.
  (b) If a fix cell HARD_FAILs with the SAME error type/class as the prior cell
      it was supposed to fix, auto-tier as HONEST_NEGATIVE_FIX_INSUFFICIENT AND
      file a META_RULE_Z violation note (escalates to USER if recurring).
  (c) Three consecutive fix attempts in the same family that all symptom-patch
      = STOP the family + redesign from spec.

COMPOSES-WITH:
  - META_RULE_J (no silent except blocks): both about facing the actual failure
    not hiding it
  - Fix #28 (verify per-arm metrics not summary verdict): the verdict-msg of a fix
    cell often claims fix-success when per-arm data shows same numerical floor
  - 'verify the referent' discipline: root-cause IS the referent; symptom is not

name: META_RULE_AA FAIRNESS-BEFORE-TIER: HARD_FAIL cells must have fairness audited before being filed as honest-negative -- 4 fairness gates (baseline / smoke power / regime / discriminator)
description:
META RULE AA (CERT-neutral; discipline_meta):

A cell that HARD_FAILs MUST have its FAIRNESS audited before the result is filed as honest-negative. Specifically:
  (a) BASELINES MUST NOT IMPLICITLY DO THE MECHANISM we're testing.       A baseline arm that already incorporates some fraction of the       mechanism (e.g. averaging the very operators a router would pick       between; ensembling readouts a Fisher selector would gate;       smoothing trajectories an attractor would correct) gives a rigged       comparison and the mechanism may be working without the lift       showing up.
  (b) SMOKE SEEDS AND N MUST BE LARGE ENOUGH to distinguish lift from       noise. Per-arm cv_sel < 0.30 is the gate (with cv > 1.0 at n=2 the       mechanism status is UNKNOWN, not NULL). Per-arm seed-level wins       hidden by aggregate means must be surfaced.
  (c) THE REGIME MUST ACTUALLY EXERCISE THE MECHANISM. Baselines that       saturate (>=0.95) make any mechanism arm look like null;       preconditions that fail (e.g. tag fraction too low for BTSP,       sequence depth too short for chains) starve the mechanism.       Pre-flight regime probe required when pre-reg specifies baseline       target band.
  (d) THE TEST DATA MUST ALLOW THE DISCRIMINATOR TO FIRE (META_RULE_K).       A discriminator that saturates all arms (top-1=1.0 across the       board) is vacuous regardless of cell.

If any of (a)-(d) is violated the verdict is NOT HONEST_NEGATIVE_SUBSTRATE -- it is TEST_DESIGN_FAILURE. Re-author + re-smoke before tiering. The mechanism status remains UNKNOWN.

WITNESS (2026-06-27 wave-1 smoke audit, 3 of 4 cells confirmed by verify-off-data):
  - pfc_controller_v1: baseline = avg of 4 operator matrices = implicit     uniform-mixture router (violation of (a)). Revival pfc_softmax_v2     with single_fixed_baseline showed lift +0.378 at depth=6 --     mechanism works cleanly.
  - multi_readout_fisher_v1: smoke n=2 cv=1.23 hid per-arm seed-17     wins (eight_readout_pca_basis +0.144; diag_k_sweep +0.300)     (violation of (b)).
  - sub_atom_encoder_v1: unbind_d3 proxy uses cos > 0.30 threshold on     short synthetic expressions -- trigram baseline saturates 1.0 along     with codebook arms (violation of (d)); depth=1 partial-positive     (codebook 1.0 vs trigram 0.0) hidden by MIDDLE_BAND framing.

name: INDETERMINATE_NEEDS_DIAGNOSTIC tonegawa_v3_BUNDLED: XOR-bundle incompatible with sparse k-WTA codes (98pct zeros -> XOR-unbind near-degenerate); PROTO=0.836 TONE=0.040 DIAG=0.044 ratio_DIAG_over_TONE=1.10; only ONE bundle op tested; additive-bind variant required
description: Wave 2H DRILL on tonegawa_v2 INDETERMINATE (morning audit). v3 implements bundled-bank regime as v2 audit specified. Verify-off-data finding: per-arm recall@1_K25 (single seed=7, N_DIM=1024, K_SCHEMAS=1024, K_SPARSE=20, BCC=0.30, WCN=0.60, K_SWEEP=[25,100]) shows ARM_PROTOTYPE_CENTROID_BUNDLED=0.836, ARM_TONEGAWA_SPARSE_K20_BUNDLED=0.040, ARM_DIAG_RANDOM_SPARSE_BUNDLED=0.044. Ratios: TONE/PROTO=0.048 (TONE 20.9x worse); DIAG/TONE=1.10 (random essentially matches structured sparse) -> structure NOT load-bearing AT THIS BUNDLE_OP. Capacity@95 all arms = 0.0 across K_SWEEP=[25,100] (no arm reaches 0.95 recall after bundling -- bundling capacity exhausted in this regime). Cell-author's claim 'both collapse at K=100' is verified, but the framing 'HRR-bundled sparse encoding genuinely uncompetitive vs dense centroid' is TOO STRONG because only XOR-bundle was tested. Architecture issue: cell defines S = sum_k XOR(schema_id_k, sparse_code_k); XOR-bind is HRR-designed for DENSE bipolar codes (roughly equal +1/-1 mass). Sparse k-WTA codes with K_SPARSE=20 out of N=1024 are ~98pct zero. XOR of two ~98pct-zero vectors is ~96pct zero (since 0 XOR 0 = 0) -> the bundled superposition S becomes ~96pct zero too -> unbinding via XOR(query, S) is near-degenerate. The mechanism's algebraic premise (XOR-unbinding distinguishes schema-bound from noise) breaks when input vectors don't have HRR's required statistics. v3 result IS a clean diagnostic: it rules out XOR-bundled-Tonegawa as a substrate-native mechanism in this regime, but does NOT rule out: (a) additive-bind variant `S = sum_k (schema_id_k + sparse_code_k)` with cleanup; (b) Plate's compress-then-bundle for sparse codes; (c) coarse-grained-position binding at smaller K_WTA support. K_SWEEP=[25,100] verifies cell-author's 'K=25 too small to favor sparse' concern is NOT the issue at K=100 -- both regimes collapse equivalently. n_seeds=1 smoke; mechanism status: UNKNOWN, NOT proven-null. 3X DRILL spec: (a) re-author with additive bundle op; (b) sweep K=[10,25,50] sparse-load depth; (c) n_seeds=5 minimum; (d) recall via top-K cleanup against schema-id codebook (no XOR-unbinding). Mechanism remains a candidate for substrate-native sparse-schema-ensemble class until additive-bind variant is tested and characterized.

CORE DESIGN FAILURE (cell-author identified, Skunkworks confirms via raw-data audit): there is NO INTERFERENCE TO SELECTIVELY RESCUE FROM. STC's mechanism is 'selectively preserve some weights during catastrophic-forgetting overwrite by tagging strong synapses during phase A so phase-B writes spare them'. If catastrophic forgetting doesn't happen (because substrate writes additively and is at 4pct of capacity), then the mechanism has no scenario to demonstrate value. Substrate write capacity estimate: M_max ~ N / proto_noise^2 ~ 1024/0.72 ~ 1400 patterns; current 50 patterns (NCAT=10 x NVAR=5) is 4pct of capacity. Cell-author's surfaced fix ('ETA_CAPTURE=0.20 lets A and B coexist additively; needs ETA_CAPTURE=1.0 or W_slow normalization') is one option but doesn't address the root cause: at this capacity regime + write mode, single B-pattern doesn't displace A-patterns regardless of ETA_CAPTURE. Mechanism status: UNKNOWN; NOT a substrate null; does NOT count against any META claim about W-update-rule. 3X DRILL spec: (a) push NCAT_phase1 + NCAT_phase2 >= 200 (force regime to substrate capacity); (b) add W_slow normalization between phases (||W||_F held constant after B-writes); (c) ETA_CAPTURE=1.0 with consolidation-pulses interleaved; (d) explicit baseline_no_stc_A_after_target=[0.40, 0.70] in HP gate (HARD_FAIL if baseline_A_after>0.70, telling cell-author the regime didn't bite).

name: META_NUANCED_PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED wave2 failure pattern: THREE distinct root-cause families (saturation / interference-absent / bundle-op-incompatible) NOT one; non-classification-readout pivot helps family A only; strong form of META overgeneralized
description: Research-surfaced META claim (Wave 2H wrap-up): 'Wave 2 mechanism tests in our substrate's prototype-classification task are subject to deeper saturation issues that 4 separate cell-author fixes can't resolve at the cell level. Pattern recommendation: pivot to non-classification readouts (capacity@retrieval, interference-fraction-measured, signal-to-crosstalk ratio).' Skunkworks vetting (verify-off-data across 9 today's Wave 2 cells): PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED_BUT_OVERGENERALIZED. The saturation pattern IS real (5 cells: tonegawa_v2 NO_SCHEMA r@k=1.000, stc_v1 all-4-arms-tied-0.953, stc_v2 baseline_A_after=0.999, cortex_E_tensor_v1 rec_old=1.000, tonegawa_v3 PROTOTYPE=0.836 just-below); the 'cell-author fixes can't resolve' claim is TOO STRONG (tonegawa_v3 DID resolve v2's bank-config mismatch by moving to bundled-bank, just exposed a NEW layer issue with XOR-bundle-incompatible-with-sparse; stc_v2 DID resolve v1's fairness-violation, just exposed deeper interference-regime-absent issue). Three distinct root-cause families CONFLATED in Research's META framing: (A) BASELINE-SATURATION (regime too easy, no readout headroom): tonegawa_v2 NO_SCHEMA, stc_v1, cortex_E_tensor_v1, stc_v2 baseline_A; (B) INTERFERENCE-REGIME-ABSENT (substrate writes additively, B doesn't displace A): stc_v2 specifically; (C) BUNDLE-OP-INCOMPATIBLE (chosen superposition op breaks algebraic premise): tonegawa_v3 specifically. Non-classification-readout recommendation: HELPS family (A) (capacity@95 instead of recall@K broke saturation ties in tonegawa_v2 to reveal 17x cap loss); does NOT help family (B) (no readout cures absent-interference-regime; need regime push to capacity or explicit W normalization); does NOT help family (C) (no readout cures algebraic-incompatibility; need additive-bind or sparse-aware bundle op). Honest framing: cell-author fixes RESOLVE Wave 2 design issues sequentially but each fix uncovers the next lower layer (fairness -> bundle-regime -> interference-regime -> bundle-op-compatibility). The 'deeper saturation' framing is half-right; actual pattern is 'sequential design-issue layers'. Non-classification-readout pivot is GOOD partial fix for family (A) but isn't a panacea. 3X DRILL META spec: verify against next 3 Wave 2 cells (stc_v3, tonegawa_v4, plus one new mechanism). If 3 consecutive fail with family (A) SPECIFICALLY AND cell-author fixes can't move past saturation, the STRONG form of META becomes supportable. Until then, atomize NUANCED version only. DO NOT atomize the over-generalized 'deeper saturation issues that fixes can't resolve' framing -- it's a CONFLATION error.

name: TEST_DESIGN_FAILURE TOT criterion rigged tip_of_tongue_v1 (HC/LC gates met; rho wrong sign; percentile-on-clean-baseline criterion can't see brain-aligned TOT state at low SNR)
description: exp_meta_knowledge_tip_of_tongue_v1_smoke verdict HARD_FAIL on rho(SNR,TOT)=+0.150 (need <=-0.7 brain-aligned) and cluster_acc_in_TOT=0.565 (need >=0.70). Per-seed SNR sweep (seed 7): TOT-rate is 0.167 / 0.267 / 0.217 / 0.417 / 0.183 at SNR=0.2/0.3/0.5/0.7/1.0 - non-monotone with peak at SNR=0.7 (brain would predict peak at LOW SNR). Seed 17: 0.233 / 0.233 / 0.333 / 0.450 / 0.067 - similar non-monotone. Root cause is the TOT operational definition (source line 91-94):   TOT case = atom_cleanup_cos < Q30(clean) AND cluster_cos > Q50(clean) where Q* are quantiles of the SNR=1.0 baseline distribution per seed. The implicit assumption is that at low SNR, cluster_cos stays high (you know the category) while cleanup_cos drops (you can't recall the specific item). In practice at the smoke regime, low-SNR queries see BOTH cluster_cos and cleanup_cos drop together - the criterion 'cluster_cos > Q50_clean' fires LESS often at low SNR even though the substrate IS in the brain-aligned 'know the category not the word' state. Cell-author fix needed: redefine TOT with ABSOLUTE thresholds (e.g., cleanup_cos below 0.5 AND cluster_cos above 0.3 - tuned per substrate calibration) or use per-SNR-bin quantiles (relative to the SNR-bin baseline, not the clean baseline). Verdict-tier: no tier change for v1 (mechanism untestable as written). Drill-trigger: 2x drill REQUIRED with redefined TOT criterion. Note this composes META_FAIRNESS_PATTERN (Wave 1 4-cell test-design failures) and META_RULE_AA fairness-before-tier.

name: META_RULE_AD: probe-band tolerance MUST absorb >= 1.96*SEM of multi-seed drift; 1-seed probe finding cfg in band does NOT reliably predict 5-seed full baseline. Witness BTSP v2.
description:
META_RULE_AD (CERT-neutral; discipline_meta; delta=0):

When a cell uses a 1-seed PROBE stage to find a hyperparameter configuration with
baseline in a target band, the probe-band tolerance MUST be widened to absorb at
least 1.96 * SEM_multi-seed of the expected multi-seed regression in that baseline.
Equivalently: probes MUST use a minimum of 3 seeds and ALL 3 must land in band
before declaring cfg-found.

FAILURE MODE: at marginal hyperparameter regimes, single-seed baseline can be
drastically different from multi-seed mean. A 1-seed probe saying 'baseline=1.0
in cfg X' cannot reliably predict that 5-seed full will produce baseline_acc in
any specific band; the variance across seeds at marginal cfg can flip baseline by
0.5+ points.

WITNESS (verified off-data 2026-06-27):
  data/exp_btsp_binary_synapse_one_shot_v2_regime_probed/metrics.json
  Single probe cfg found: N=2048, NCAT=100, NTRAIN=10, noise=0.85, alpha=0.0488
    -> probe baseline_acc = 1.000 (OUTSIDE band [0.40, 0.65] by ceiling)
  found_cfg = null (no cfg in band)
  verdict = HARD_FAIL with REGIME_INFEASIBLE message
  Cell halted at probe stage; no mechanism arm ran.
  The probe failure is two-fold: (a) only one cfg point tested (single point in
  5-D hyperparameter space), AND (b) even that cfg's 1-seed baseline=1.0 does not
  necessarily reflect 5-seed multi-seed regression behavior.

PROPOSED ENFORCEMENT (Skunkworks SCHEMA-VET):
  Pre-reg cells with probe stages MUST include:
    (1) N_PROBE_SEEDS >= 3 (typically 3-5)
    (2) PROBE_BAND_TOLERANCE that absorbs >= 1.96 * expected SEM
    (3) PROBE_GRID minimum 4 cfg points (not single-point sweep)
    (4) declared cfg-found ONLY if ALL probe seeds land in band
  SCHEMA-VET rejects probe cells missing (1)-(4) at pre-reg time.

COMPOSES-WITH: META_RULE_AA (fairness-before-tier; baseline-must-be-in-band), Fix
#28 (verify per-arm not summary-text), USER experiment bias master checklist BIAS-2
(single-seed cherry-pick risk).

name: META_RULE_AF: multi-arm cells MUST include self-test that arm outputs are NOT bit-identical; pattern hash(arm_a.output) != hash(arm_b.output). Witness parietal v1 REL aliased to MOVABLE.
description:
META_RULE_AF (CERT-neutral; discipline_meta; delta=0):

Multi-arm cells MUST include a self-test assertion that arm outputs are NOT bit-
identical across arms claimed to test different mechanisms. The arm-aliasing failure
(two arms producing identical output across all seeds) is a SILENT cell bug that
passes cardinality, passes discriminator checks (if you only look at one arm), and
produces seemingly-clean metrics -- but the 'comparison' between the two arms is
vacuous because they're the same computation.

PATTERN (suggested implementation):
  for (arm_a_name, arm_a), (arm_b_name, arm_b) in itertools.combinations(
      claimed_mechanism_arms.items(), 2):
    assert hash(arm_a.output_tensor.tobytes()) != hash(arm_b.output_tensor.tobytes()), \
      f'Arm {arm_a_name} bit-identical to {arm_b_name} -- not testing distinct mechanism'

WITNESS (already filed as research_flag note):
  notes/research_flag_parietal_REL_arm_bit_identical_to_MOVABLE_cell_bug_2026-06-27.md
  data/exp_parietal_cortex_spatial_reasoning_v1/metrics.json shows:
    grid_position_with_relations (REL arm) bit-identical to grid_position_movable
    (MOVABLE arm) across ALL 5 seeds (seeds 7, 17, 23, 31, 41). Every per-arm field
    matches: position_recall, move_recall, relational_recall all identical to 4
    decimal places per seed.
  Skunkworks atomized parietal MOVABLE as CHAIN_GRADE (2026-06-27) but REL as
    HONEST_NEGATIVE relational-arm-aliased; the cell-author's relational mechanism
    is not actually differentiated as a distinct testable pathway.

ENFORCEMENT (Skunkworks SCHEMA-VET):
  Pre-reg cells with >=2 arms claimed to test distinct mechanisms MUST include
  arms_distinct_self_test code OR explicit declaration that arms ARE expected to
  alias (e.g. control arm intentionally identical to baseline for sanity check).
  SCHEMA-VET rejects multi-arm cells missing this gate.

  Skunkworks landed-VET: when a multi-arm cell lands, perform arm-aliasing audit
  on per_arm metrics blocks; flag aliased arms as cell-bug requiring v2 fix BEFORE
  tiering any of the cell's arms as chain-grade.

COMPOSES-WITH: META_RULE_T (per-arm verification), META_RULE_AC (HYPOTHESIZED-vs-
MEASURED -- aliased arms produce HYP-only mechanism claims), Fix #28.

name: META_RULE_AH: substrate compositional reasoning at depth=5 ALREADY chain-grade -- Barrier 1 was a FAKE ceiling. Per-hop argmax cleanup baseline reaches 58% at depth=5 WITHOUT brain-pushback mechanism.
description:
META_RULE_AH (CERT-neutral; discipline_meta; delta=0):

The 'Barrier 1: substrate cannot compose beyond depth-2' narrative (cited in prior
QUADRUPLE_NEGATIVE META atom relabel; cited in various drill notes 2026-06-25 to
2026-06-27) is FALSIFIED by the substrate_multihop_brain_pushback_v3 measurement
(this batch ATOM 1 chain-grade). Substrate per-hop argmax cleanup primitive ALONE
achieves 5-hop compositional recall at 56-61% (mean 58%) across 3 seeds at production
scale (N=8192, V_C=1000, N_chains=200).

WHAT THIS MEANS:
  (1) Future drill notes that frame multi-hop compositional reasoning as 'substrate
      cannot do this; need brain pushback' are WRONG at the framing level.
  (2) Brain-pushback mechanisms (R1 replay, R2 PFC scratchpad, R3 bidirectional)
      can still ADD VALUE -- but ONLY at regimes where baseline is NOT at ceiling.
      Composes with META_RULE_AG (substrate-too-robust-for-mechanism-at-default-
      regime; this batch ATOM 10): mechanism comparison must push substrate to
      EDGE OF CAPACITY where baseline drops into [0.30, 0.70] band before mechanism
      arms can show lift.
  (3) The 'Barrier 1' framing was load-bearing for the 7-mechanism multi-hop drill
      (2026-06-25). That drill's claim 'substrate stuck at 2-hop ceiling' is
      REFUTED at production scale; the drill should be revised to focus on:
      (a) capacity-edge regimes where mechanism lift matters,
      (b) deeper-than-5 chains where baseline does drop,
      (c) different chain types (heterogeneous predicates, longer-distance bindings).
  (4) Stage 3 (per USER stage progression 1->2->3->4 LOCKED 2026-06-26) is now
      partially demonstrated -- not by brain-pushback mechanism but by primitive
      substrate operation. This is GOOD news for substrate-as-product narrative.

RATIFIED FRAMING (replaces prior 'Barrier 1' framing):
  'Substrate per-hop argmax-cleanup primitive achieves 5-hop compositional retrieval
   at 58% (chain-grade, cv=0.036 at production scale). Brain-pushback mechanisms
   add value ONLY at capacity-edge regimes; default regime tests are mechanism-
   irrelevant by substrate-too-robust pattern (see META_RULE_AG, ATOM 10 this batch).'

EVIDENCE: this batch ATOM 1 (chain-grade substrate depth-5 compositional).
EVIDENCE METRICS: data/exp_substrate_multihop_brain_pushback_v3_redispatch/metrics.json

COMPOSES-WITH:
  - ATOM 1 (CHAIN_GRADE substrate depth-5 compositional, this batch)
  - META_RULE_AG (substrate-too-robust-for-default-regime, this batch ATOM 10)
  - prior META_BARRIER_1_QUADRUPLE_NEGATIVE relabel atom (2026-06-27 earlier batch)
  - META_RULE_T (per-arm verification before META atomization)
  - META_RULE_AC (HYPOTHESIZED-vs-MEASURED; this batch ATOM 4)

RECTIFICATION TARGET: any drill / spawn / framing using 'Barrier 1 substrate cannot
compose at depth>2' should cite this META_RULE_AH and revise framing accordingly.

name: META_RULE_AI: RAIL_SANITY_BREACH when baseline >> predicted-high should be reinterpreted as substrate-exceeds-prediction (not experiment broken). Witness Cycle 1 v3+v4 both breach upward.
description:
META_RULE_AI (CERT-neutral; discipline_meta; delta=0):

When a cell's pre-reg predicts baseline in band [low, high] and the observed baseline
is SUBSTANTIALLY above [high] (e.g. by >2x or by >0.30 absolute), the verdict
RAIL_SANITY_BREACH should be RE-INTERPRETED as 'substrate exceeds prediction', NOT
as 'experiment broken'. Test design needs a NEW (wider, higher) baseline_rail, not
a new mechanism.

Failure mode being corrected: cell-authors / Director sometimes treat RAIL_SANITY
as a negative finding (mechanism failed to land in expected regime) when in fact the
substrate is performing BETTER than predicted at the BASELINE arm -- a positive
substrate finding that the test design wasn't ready to interpret.

DECISION RULE (Skunkworks landed-VET):
  When verdict == RAIL_SANITY_BREACH:
    Check: is observed baseline > predicted-high BY MORE THAN baseline_rail width?
    If yes: RE-INTERPRET as 'substrate-exceeds-prediction'; this is positive data
      about substrate capability; mechanism comparison may still be meaningful but
      at a DIFFERENT effective regime than pre-registered.
    If no: standard RAIL_SANITY_BREACH (experiment broken; cfg drift; bug).

CONCRETE WITNESSES (verified off-data 2026-06-27):
  (a) substrate_multihop_brain_pushback_v3_redispatch:
      data/exp_substrate_multihop_brain_pushback_v3_redispatch/metrics.json
      Pre-reg baseline_rail = [0.10, 0.20]; observed BASELINE@d5 = 0.582
      Excess over [high] = 0.582 - 0.20 = +0.382 (>> baseline_rail width 0.10)
      Substrate-EXCEEDS-prediction at the baseline arm; chain-grade-eligible as
      ATOM 1 this batch.
  (b) substrate_multihop_brain_pushback_composition_v4_harder_regime_smoke:
      data/exp_substrate_multihop_brain_pushback_composition_v4_harder_regime_smoke/metrics.json
      Pre-reg baseline_rail = [0.10, 0.30]; observed BASELINE@d5 = 0.875
      Excess over [high] = 0.875 - 0.30 = +0.575 (>> baseline_rail width 0.20)
      Substrate-EXCEEDS-prediction at smoke scale; confirms (a) at smaller N.

ENFORCEMENT (Skunkworks landed-VET protocol addition):
  For RAIL_SANITY_BREACH verdicts, compute baseline_excess_over_high = observed -
  predicted_high. If excess > baseline_rail_width, tag as 'substrate-exceeds-prediction'
  and route the BASELINE arm for tier consideration on its own merit (not the
  mechanism-vs-baseline comparison which is at the wrong regime).

COMPOSES-WITH:
  - META_RULE_AG (substrate-too-robust-for-mechanism-at-default-regime; this batch
    ATOM 10): same root cause -- mechanism comparison fails because substrate ALREADY
    SATURATES the test region.
  - META_RULE_AH (Barrier 1 was fake; this batch ATOM 8): downstream framing
    revision.
  - META_RULE_T (per-arm verification before META atomization).

name: META_RULE_AG: substrate-too-robust-for-mechanism-at-default-regime. When test design picks default-regime parameters, substrate primitives saturate baseline leaving NO headroom for mechanism. Witness Cycle 1 v3+v4.
description:
META_RULE_AG (CERT-neutral; discipline_meta; delta=0):

When test design picks DEFAULT-regime parameters for a 'substrate baseline vs
mechanism' comparison, substrate's primitive cleanup operations are ROBUST ENOUGH
to saturate baseline at chain-grade-quality levels, leaving NO HEADROOM for
mechanism arms to lift. Mechanism arms tie baseline (or lose slightly), masking
real mechanism value.

WITNESS (1 case, verified off-data 2026-06-27):
  Cycle 1 multihop brain-pushback v3 + v4 (same cell family, two scales):
    v3 FULL data/exp_substrate_multihop_brain_pushback_v3_redispatch/metrics.json:
      BASELINE_depth_5 = 0.582 (mean across 3 seeds)
      All 5 arms (BASELINE + R1 + R2 + R3 + COMBINED) IDENTICAL within seed:
        seed=7: ALL = 0.610  seed=17: ALL = 0.560  seed=23: ALL = 0.575
      Substrate per-hop argmax cleanup is ceiling-bound; mechanisms tie baseline.
    v4 SMOKE data/exp_substrate_multihop_brain_pushback_composition_v4_harder_regime_smoke/metrics.json:
      BASELINE_depth_5 = 0.875 (1 seed; smaller N=2048, larger V_C=2000)
      All 5 arms also identical (all 0.875 at seed=7)
    Cell-author diagnosis (verbatim from notes): 'cleanup mechanism may need to be
      the variable, not the data density.'

  NOTE: sws_rem v2 was initially flagged as a second witness; coordinator correction
  2026-06-27 reframes that cell as a clean HONEST_NEGATIVE (this batch ATOM 3),
  not C7 evidence: CONST baseline IS in [0.30, 0.70] band, discriminator DID fire,
  cyclic arms simply LOSE -- substrate-product negative, not test-design failure.

PATTERN: 'substrate is too robust for the regime' = mechanism-vs-baseline lift is
trivially zero because baseline already does the task well. NOT a mechanism failure;
NOT a test-design failure; an architectural insight that the test must push to the
EDGE of substrate capacity for mechanism comparison to be informative.

ENFORCEMENT (Skunkworks SCHEMA-VET protocol addition):
  Pre-reg smoke discipline should INCLUDE a baseline-in-band check at FULL scale
  (not just smoke). If baseline lands outside the discriminating band [low, high]
  at full scale, mechanism comparison is meaningless -- REGIME-FIRST design is
  required:
    (1) Pick capacity-axis variable (V_C, N_chains, depth, N_DIM, etc.)
    (2) Find regime where baseline lands in [0.30, 0.70] discriminating band
    (3) THEN compare mechanisms in that regime
  Otherwise the cell tests 'mechanism beats trivial-task baseline' (uninformative).

SUBSTRATE-PRODUCT FRAMING (load-bearing for product narrative):
  This is GOOD news for substrate (primitives are robust). Brain-pushback mechanisms
  aren't broken; they just have NO ROOM to add value at default regimes. Future cell
  designs need REGIME-FIRST authoring: pick the regime where baseline lands in the
  discriminating band [0.30, 0.70], THEN compare mechanisms. Otherwise it's not
  testing mechanisms -- it's confirming substrate primitives are good.

COMPOSES-WITH:
  - META_RULE_AA (fairness-before-tier; Skunkworks inst 248): baseline-must-be-in-band
    precondition.
  - META_RULE_AI (RAIL_SANITY_BREACH means substrate-exceeds-prediction; this batch
    ATOM 9): same root pattern at the verdict level.
  - META_RULE_AH (Barrier 1 was fake; this batch ATOM 8): downstream framing
    revision.
  - ATOM 1 this batch (CHAIN_GRADE substrate depth-5 compositional): the positive
    substrate finding this rule emerges from.

name: META_RULE_AJ: scheduled-task registration MUST be VERIFIED end-to-end (registration + first scan output), not assumed from memory file existence. Witness landing_notifier 4-day silent drift.
description:
META_RULE_AJ (CERT-neutral; discipline_meta; delta=0):

When a memory rule (Fix #25 et al.) declares that a scheduled task SHOULD be running
periodically, the existence of the rule in memory.md is NOT sufficient evidence that
the task IS running. Scheduled-task registration MUST be VERIFIED end-to-end via:
  (1) schtasks /query /tn <task_name> /fo LIST (PowerShell; bash mangles /query)
      -> confirms task is registered
  (2) Inspect task's most recent run output file (logs / data appended by task)
      -> confirms task is firing AND producing expected output
  (3) If output file doesn't exist or last-updated > task interval * 2, declare
      DRIFT and re-register / debug

WITNESS (root cause of 3 phantom-vet batches 2026-06-27):
  Per Fix #25 (memory rule 2026-06-22): landing_notifier scheduled task should have
  been running every 2-5 min appending to data/recent_landings.jsonl. It was NEVER
  REGISTERED. 4 days of silent drift during the autonomous arc.
  Symptom: Director repeatedly missed remote landings because filesystem poll-for-
  landings (Fix #21) had no notifier to consult. Director relied on stale recent_
  landings.jsonl that was never being appended.
  Discovery 2026-06-27: Orchestrator a283a14a registered the task fresh; 663 backlog
  landings flushed in the first scan window.

ENFORCEMENT (testbed FLEET-HEALTH discipline + Director session-start ritual):
  (a) Session-start ritual: after arming Monitor (CLAUDE.md STEP 1), Director runs
      schtasks /query for every Fix-N-declared scheduled task + checks last-updated
      timestamp on its expected output file. If drift detected, re-register before
      proceeding.
  (b) MEMORY.md memory-rule format extension: every Fix-N rule declaring a scheduled
      task MUST include:
        - exact schtasks command to register
        - exact schtasks /query verification command
        - expected output file path with expected update interval
      Without all three, the rule is INCOMPLETE.
  (c) Testbed FLEET-HEALTH audits include scheduled-task drift as a check item.

COMPOSES-WITH: Fix #21 (poll filesystem for remote-landed cells; depended on this
task), Fix #25 (landing notifier scheduled task; the failing instance), USER directive
'no busy work / single-session dispatch' (silent drift wastes hours).

name: META_RULE_AK: cell templates MUST have `except SystemExit: raise` BEFORE `except BaseException`. Witness trigram_downstream cell + 2 metrics.json sentinel overwrites.
description:
META_RULE_AK (CERT-neutral; discipline_meta; delta=0):

Cell templates that have a top-level try/except BaseException block (for graceful
import-crash sentinel writing) MUST include `except SystemExit: raise` BEFORE the
BaseException handler. Otherwise the legitimate SystemExit(0) emitted by sys.exit(0)
at end of successful main() execution is CAUGHT by BaseException, treated as an
import-crash, and the metrics.json is overwritten with an import-crash sentinel --
destroying the successful science output.

PATTERN:
  try:
      main()  # may sys.exit(0) at end
  except SystemExit:                    # MUST come FIRST
      raise                              # propagate clean exit
  except BaseException as e:            # catches REAL import crashes only
      write_import_crash_sentinel(e)
      raise

WITNESS (narrow scope, but caught by Orchestrator a4cc90c0 patch 2026-06-27):
  trigram_downstream cell had the bug. Sweep of all data/*/metrics.json found 2 files
  affected (both same anchor; narrow scope -- only that cell variant).
  Symptom: successful main() ran, science metrics computed, sys.exit(0) called,
  BaseException handler caught it, overwrote metrics.json with sentinel. Cell
  appeared to FAIL but science results were valid up until the overwrite.
  Fix: patched cell template with `except SystemExit: raise` block.

ENFORCEMENT (Skunkworks SCHEMA-VET extension):
  Pre-reg cells using import-crash sentinel pattern MUST have the SystemExit-before-
  BaseException ordering. SCHEMA-VET checks for the pattern in cell source before
  approving dispatch. testbed FLEET-HEALTH audit periodically greps experiments/
  for missing-SystemExit-handler patterns.

COMPOSES-WITH:
  - META_RULE_J (no-silent-except blocks; record+halt OR re-raise): same root
    discipline (BaseException-without-SystemExit-handling is silent-except for the
    SystemExit case).
  - Three smoke disciplines 2026-06-26 memory rule (no silent except).

name: META_RULE_AL substrate-cosine-kernel pre-encodes schema-prior information: explicit schema-prior mechanisms (context-bound priors, vmPFC-prior, etc.) yield no additive lift when substrate cosine geometry already encodes the schema-discriminative axes
description:
META_RULE_AL substrate-cosine-kernel pre-encodes schema-prior (discipline atom; delta=0).
When the substrate codebook is trained or encoded such that schema-aligned items
cluster along cosine-discriminative axes, explicit schema-prior mechanisms (e.g.
HRR-bound context priors, sequential-prior composition) recover the SAME information
via a different operation and yield no additive lift when composed with the implicit
kernel-encoded prior.

EVIDENCE (chain-of-occurrence; 3rd today per Director batch context):
  Occurrence 3 (cleanly atomized in this batch -- ATOM 3 above):
    cortex_schema_instantiation_context_prior_v1 [smoke; verified off data]
      ARM_CONTEXT_BOUND_PRIOR  recall=0.731
      ARM_EXEMPLAR_BAYES_K20   recall=0.728
      lift_over_exemplar       =+0.003 (essentially zero)
      ARM_HYBRID_PRIOR_PLUS_EXEMPLAR recall=0.730
      hybrid_lift_over_primary =-0.001 (no additive composition)
      ARM_RANDOM_PRIOR         recall=0.119 (control: mechanism IS firing)
    -> CONTEXT_BOUND_PRIOR mechanism is real (vs random) but recovers same info as
       EXEMPLAR_BAYES via different operation; HYBRID adds nothing.
  Occurrences 1 + 2 (Director-reported earlier today; not yet atomized at this batch
    layer): substrate-cosine-already-discriminates findings in prior smoke results;
    cell anchors pending future batch consolidation.

RULE STATEMENT:
  IF substrate codebook is trained/encoded such that schema-aligned items cluster
     along cosine-discriminative axes (cosine kernel is 'schema-aware'),
  AND a candidate mechanism M aims to add explicit schema-prior information,
  THEN M will show high recall (because it exploits the same underlying signal)
     BUT M will NOT yield additive lift over a cosine-similarity baseline
     (because the baseline already captures what M tries to add).
  CORRECTIVE: test M on an encoder/codebook where cosine kernel is NOT schema-aware
     (random projection, untrained encoder, hash-trick) to demonstrate M's marginal
     contribution; OR design discriminator that fires only when explicit-prior beats
     cosine-baseline by mechanistic margin (not just absolute recall).

WHEN TO INVOKE:
  - Pre-reg vetting: any cell claiming 'explicit schema-prior mechanism adds X'
    on a cosine-similarity substrate must include the non-schema-aware-kernel arm
    OR explicitly mark the expected-lift as cosine-vs-explicit not random-vs-explicit.
  - Cert-tier review: an 'explicit schema-prior' result that shows lift only over
    random-prior (not over cosine-baseline) is MEASURED_MECHANISM at best, not
    chain-grade evidence for the explicit-prior mechanism.

RELATIONSHIP TO PRIOR META_RULES:
  - Complements META_RULE_AG (substrate-too-robust-for-mechanism-at-default-regime):
    that rule covers substrate being above-ceiling for the mechanism to add lift;
    THIS rule covers substrate cosine-kernel pre-encoding the mechanism's signal.
    Both are 'substrate-already-does-X' findings; AG is regime-driven, AL is
    kernel-geometry-driven.
  - Composes with experiment-bias master checklist Q (suspect 1.000 results) +
    P (anisotropy-hurts-retrieval Mu-Viswanath): cosine kernel that encodes schema
    creates anisotropic structure that downstream mechanisms exploit.

DISCIPLINE STATUS: NEUTRAL meta-rule (no cert increment). Tracked for application
in future schema-prior / explicit-prior cell pre-reg vetting.

description:
META_RULE_AM substrate-already-does-X test discipline (discipline atom; delta=0).
Process-layer extension of META_RULE_AL (substrate-cosine pre-encodes schema-prior).

     (data/exp_schema_inference_cross_schema_overlap_sweep_v1_smoke/metrics.json):

  5. Hierarchical planning v1

  6. Self-explanation v1+v2
     (data/exp_self_explanation_deletion_fidelity_v{1,2}_*_smoke/metrics.json):
     Bind-trace (v1 bilinear=0.240; v2 marginal=0.026) LOSES to raw COSINE

  7. Narrative event-segmentation (cross-link to ATOM 3 this batch)
     (data/exp_stage3_narrative_coherence_100event_5char_full_stack_v1/metrics.json):
     ARM_NO_SEGMENT=0.556 TIES ARM_FULL_STACK=0.556 (lift 0.000); predicted_sha16
     IDENTICAL across all 3 seeds. Event-segmentation primitive NOT load-bearing
     at K_active=51 / alpha=0.05 / 100-event regime.

  8. Boundary detector at drill regime (cross-link to ATOM 5 this batch)
     (data/exp_stage3_narrative_event_boundary_detector_only_v1/metrics.json):

name: META_RULE_AN cone-collapse-formula-N2048-calibrated: crosstalk_std=sqrt((V_C_per_hop-1)/N) calibrated at N=2048 does NOT naively extrapolate to N=8192; substrate has ~3.7x MORE headroom at larger N than linear cone model predicts; recalibration required before using formula to design cells at N>2048; extends META_RULE_AL at capacity layer
description:
META_RULE_AN: META discipline atom (delta=0). Substrate-product process rule landed
after Skunkworks batch 15 verify-off-data on Stage 3 morning revival wave (Atom 2
above provides the concrete evidence).

RULE STATEMENT:
  The cone-collapse formula crosstalk_std = sqrt((V_C_per_hop - 1) / N) is calibrated
  EMPIRICALLY at N=2048 and CANNOT be naively extrapolated to N>=8192 to predict
  baseline top1 at depth-d multi-hop cleanup. Substrate has substantially more
  effective headroom at larger N than the linear-in-(V_C/N) cone model implies;
  any cell designed using the formula at N>=8192 to set BASELINE rails must include
  an EMPIRICAL recalibration arm (e.g. a baseline-only smoke at the target N before
  the mechanism arms are dispatched) so the rails are tight.

EVIDENCE (off-disk; from batch 15 Atoms 1 and 2):
  At N=2048 V_C=1000 depth=10 (Atom 1):
    Formula predicted BASELINE top1 ~ 0.160; observed 0.190 (in rail [0.110, 0.210]).
    Formula tight.
  At N=8192 V_C=4000 depth=10 (Atom 2):
    Formula predicted BASELINE top1 ~ 0.160 (RAIL set to [0.110, 0.250] explicitly
    using the v1 calibration); observed 0.590.
    Rail breached UPWARD by factor 0.590/0.160 ~ 3.7x.
  Mechanism arms (ORACLE_B/C/D) all saturated at 1.000/1.000/0.990 -- the saturation
  itself prevents chain-grade promotion in the c1 N=8192 attempt; without the formula
  miscalibration the RAIL would have been set in [0.40, 0.80] (matching observed) and
  the un-saturated mechanism band would have been pushed to [0.85, 0.99].

CANDIDATE ROOT CAUSE (research-owned to investigate; cert-owner does NOT prescribe):
  Per-hop attrition is not linear in (V_C/N) ratio at the scale tested. Either:
  (a) Effective decoder margin has sub-linear N dependence due to angular density
      of substrate basis at higher N (cone vertex isn't the binding constraint).
  (b) The cleanup operator has a fixed-point absorption term not modeled by per-hop
      crosstalk_std.
  (c) V_C scaling (1000 -> 4000) compensates the N scaling (2048 -> 8192) less than
      1:1, but the cleanup tail is sub-Gaussian in the regime tested.

DISCIPLINE IMPLICATION:
  Before dispatching a v5-revival OR any cell using cone-collapse to set RAILS at
  N >= 4096:
    REQUIRED: run a baseline-only single-arm smoke (e.g. arm_a equivalent) at the
    target N first to empirically determine BASELINE top1 + set RAIL [BASELINE +/-
    band] EMPIRICALLY rather than from formula.
    OR: include the baseline arm as part of the smoke and treat RAIL pre-check as
    a guard not as a HP/HF gate when formula confidence is unverified at the N scale.

RELATION TO OTHER META RULES:
  Extends META_RULE_AL (substrate cosine kernel pre-encodes schema prior) at the
  capacity layer: just as cosine geometry already-aligns schemas, substrate per-hop
  cleanup already-resolves more multi-hop crosstalk at scale than the simple cone
  model captures.
  Extends META_RULE_AM (substrate-already-does-X test discipline) at the formula
  layer: substrate-already-does-X applies not just to mechanism cells but to the

  Companion to META_RULE_AH (atomic metrics): in this case the atomic per-hop top1
  per-step accuracy lists (e.g. [0.96, 0.92, 0.86, ..., 0.59] at N=8192 baseline)
  immediately show the substrate retains substantially more per-hop accuracy at
  larger N than the formula assumes.

description: When three consecutive smoke HARD_FAILs land on the same capability across DISTINCT mechanism classes (not iterations of the same mechanism), the capability box at the current substrate regime closes. File a capability-closed atom; do not iterate a 4th time without USER + research consensus on a fundamentally new mechanism class (typically a substrate-product pivot like pretrained-encoder swap-in or block-sparse codes, NOT another variation on the same encoding). The closure is OFFICIAL at the 3rd HF if (a) all 3 cells satisfy arms_distinct + cardinality_ok + discriminator-survives-scale, and (b) the 3 cells span distinct mechanism classes (e.g. closed-form vs iterative-policy vs option-framework), and (c) the diagnoses converge on a substrate-encoding root cause rather than mechanism-specific failure. Pre-reg the THIRD-FAILURE GATE in the 3rd cell so closure triggers at smoke time without requiring full dispatch. Witness 2026-06-28: hierarchical-planning closed across closed-form D_macro pseudoinverse + state-conditioned+disjoint + Sutton-Precup 1999 options pi/beta/I; all 3 cells arms_distinct + cardinality_ok + N=8192 + composite-depth=6; all converge on substrate sum-encoded HRR not preserving compositional partial-progress signal. name: META_RULE_AP -- composition of chain-grade primitives requires signal-shape compatibility audit OR explicit adapter OR co-training; naive pipe-A-into-B breaks when A's natural output shape does not match B's natural input shape
description: META_RULE_AP (composition-discipline at primitive-composition layer): Chain-grade primitives are NOT trivially composable. Each chain-grade primitive was trained / validated with a specific signal structure (specific input cue shape, specific state representation, specific regime). Piping primitive A's output into primitive B's input may break B because A's output does NOT match B's expected input signal structure. Composition requires at least ONE of: (1) explicit signal-shape adapter mechanism between A and B (learned projection,     classifier head, attention readout, etc.); (2) co-training of the composition (A and B trained jointly on the downstream task); (3) pre-cell signal-shape compatibility audit verifying A's NATURAL output signal     shape matches B's NATURAL input signal shape (cue type, dimensionality,     representation basis, variance regime). PRE-CELL DISCIPLINE (cell-author + Skunkworks SCHEMA-VET): when a cell proposes to COMPOSE 2+ chain-grade primitives, the prereg must explicitly state (a) the natural output signal shape of each upstream primitive, (b) the natural input signal shape of each downstream primitive, (c) the compatibility argument OR the adapter mechanism. Pre-reg lacking this triggers SCHEMA-VET REJECT pending compatibility audit. WITNESS 1 (atomized 2026-06-28): exp_substrate_partition_oracle_substrate_derived_hint_v1_seed_7 HARD_FAIL: naive composition of chain-grade partition-routing primitive (M=10M routing_acc=0.97 with DEDICATED category cue c_p) into multihop chain query (NO category cue) via centroid argmax fired at chance (route_acc=0.2173 vs 1/5=0.20). The parent primitive's natural input is (E[s] * R[p_rel] * c_p * sq) -- a cue-augmented binding. The multihop query natural output is (E[s] * R[p_rel] * sq) -- no category cue. Signal shapes incompatible. Naive centroid C[p]=normalize(mean(E_part[p] @ W)) does NOT bridge the gap; centroid signature is washed out by atom-level + relation-level variance. Extends META_RULE_AM (substrate-already-does-X) at the COMPOSITION layer: AM forces demonstration that existing primitive FAILS before adding new mechanism; AP forces demonstration that downstream primitive's input requirements are SATISFIED by upstream primitive's output BEFORE composing them. Related but distinct from: - META_RULE_AL (cosine kernel pre-encodes schema prior): about substrate primitive   doing X already; AP is about TWO primitives not composing. - META_RULE_AN (cone-collapse formula scaling): about REGIME extrapolation; AP is   about REPRESENTATION compatibility. - META_RULE_AO (3-HF capability closure): about KNOWING when to stop; AP is about   designing compositions correctly to avoid spurious HF on real capability.

name: META_RULE_AQ -- brain-grounded multi-primitive compositions for multi-hop / multi-step capabilities require an EXPLICIT STATE-TRACKER primitive (per-step working-memory of accumulated context) that re-fires upstream primitives per step; single-shot composition fails when fire-once assumption mismatches iterated test regime
description: META_RULE_AQ (composition-discipline at iteration layer; extends AP at composition layer): Brain-grounded multi-primitive compositions proposed for multi-step capabilities (multi-hop chains, multi-turn reasoning, multi-step plans, etc.) MUST include an explicit STATE-TRACKER primitive that maintains per-step working memory of accumulated context AND re-fires the upstream primitives per step with updated query context. Single-shot composition (fire-once-decide-once-use-decision-N-times) fails when the test regime requires N sequential decisions because static decisions cannot track the N-hop trajectory. BRAIN GROUNDING (load-bearing): brain anatomy for multi-hop reasoning has a 4-primitive circuit: (1) vmPFC schema-Bayes (cortex schema prototype matching; CITED@OReilly2014); (2) cortex partition activation (schema-conditioned routing; CITED@Mante2013); (3) hippo pattern completion (Marr 1971); (4) dorsolateral PFC working memory (MAINTAINS current-hop state and RE-FIRES     primitives 1-3 per hop with updated context; CITED@GoldmanRakic1995 +     CITED@MillerCohen2001). The cited 3 primitives are necessary but NOT SUFFICIENT for multi-hop chains. Compositions that omit primitive (4) are structurally limited to single-shot decisions. PRE-CELL DISCIPLINE (cell-author + Skunkworks SCHEMA-VET): when a cell proposes to compose multiple primitives for a MULTI-STEP capability test (multi-hop chain, multi-turn reasoning, multi-step plan, etc.), the prereg must explicitly state (a) the iteration regime (N steps; per-step target distribution); (b) which primitive maintains per-step state; (c) which primitive re-fires upstream primitives per step with updated context; (d) the structural argument that the composition CAN produce N distinct decisions     rather than ONE decision used N times. Pre-reg lacking (b)+(c)+(d) triggers SCHEMA-VET REJECT pending state-tracker addition. WITNESS 1 (atomized 2026-06-28): exp_substrate_partition_oracle_brain_composition_hint_v1_seed_7 HARD_FAIL: 3-primitive composition (vmPFC schema-Bayes + cortex partition + hippo cleanup) fires schema ONCE per chain (schema = bipolar(sum-of-all-15-predicates)), decides partition ONCE via cortex argmax, runs hippo cleanup 15 times with SAME chosen_part. Test regime requires 15 distinct per-hop partition decisions. Observed partition-correct-per-step = 0.2093 (vs 1/5 chance = 0.20); arm_c top1 = 0.01. Substrate HAS a chain-grade state-tracker primitive (WM multi-bank K=4096) but the 3-primitive composition did NOT include it. RELATION TO OTHER META_RULES: - Extends META_RULE_AP (composition signal-shape adapter) at the ITERATION layer:   AP addresses primitive-to-primitive compatibility within ONE step; AQ addresses   composition closure under iteration across N steps. Both apply when composing   chain-grade primitives -- AP for shape, AQ for iteration. - Distinct from META_RULE_AO (3-HF capability closure): AO is about knowing when   to stop iterating on a capability box; AQ is about correct composition design   for capabilities that REQUIRE iteration. - Distinct from META_RULE_AM (substrate-already-does-X): AM forces demonstration   that existing primitive FAILS before adding mechanism; AQ forces demonstration   that proposed composition has structural state-tracking primitive for iteration. M3 IMPLICATION: M3 cortex layer's compositional reasoning capability requires explicit state-tracker primitive in any multi-step composition. Substrate has the primitive (WM multi-bank) -- it just needs to be INCLUDED in compositions, not omitted. Path 2 v2 should add WM-bank as 4th primitive.

name: META_RULE_AP v3 -- chain-grade primitives not trivially composable (PROMOTED CONFIRMED with NATIVE_OUTPUT_GRANULARITY clause; 4 witnesses 2026-06-28)
description: META_RULE_AP v3 promotion to fully chain-grade CONFIRMED with new NATIVE_OUTPUT_GRANULARITY clause. Discipline statement: (v1) Chain-grade primitives do not trivially compose into a chain-grade multi-primitive pipeline; SHAPE_MATCH + capacity-feasible at every edge are NECESSARY but not SUFFICIENT for end-to-end capability to emerge. (v2 amendment, this atom NATIVE_OUTPUT_GRANULARITY clause): Primitives compose only if their NATIVE output granularity matches the downstream primitive's expected INPUT granularity. Redesigning the upstream primitive's READOUT does NOT rescue composition if the underlying TRAINING DISTRIBUTION encodes the wrong granularity. Witness pattern 2026-06-28 (4 witnesses): (1) Path 1 partition-oracle brain-composition-hint HF: schema-Bayes + cortex-routing edges SHAPE_MATCH but per-hop discrimination below floor; (2) Path 2 partition-oracle per-chain-schema HF: schema fires once per chain; partition signal pinned to hop-0; (3) Drill A PFC-WM state-tracker HF: state injection cannot rescue when cluster_to_target_part[k] map is hop-0-locked (root cause is the cluster->partition map granularity, not the absence of state); (4) Drill B per-hop schema-Bayes redesign HF: even redesigning the primitive's output via per-(cluster,hop) trajectory store does NOT rescue if the underlying schema-Bayes training distribution does not learn partial-prefix cluster identity (the PRIMITIVE'S native output is full-chain cluster-id, not partial-prefix cluster-id; downstream consumer needs partial-prefix). Practical implications: (a) Before any 4-primitive composition cell, audit each edge for TRAINING DISTRIBUTION granularity match (NOT just inference-time SHAPE_MATCH); (b) If output-granularity mismatch is structural to the primitive (as in schema-Bayes full-chain vs partial-prefix), no readout redesign at the consumer side will fix it; the granularity must be addressed at the SOURCE primitive (re-train OR new primitive class); (c) The 2x-drill discipline applied at MECHANISM CLASS level (state-tracker injection vs primitive output redesign) is the correct closure pattern for this rule; both classes failing on the same capability is structural evidence the primitive set itself is the bottleneck. Composes with META_RULE_AO (3-mechanism-class HF closure) at the MULTI-CELL aggregation layer; AP-v3 fires at the per-cell smoke discriminator-design layer.

name: META OBS: NREM-replay wall-cost ratio ~973x vs no-replay arm at N_replay=50, M=200, N_c=8192 (cortex-hippo handoff)
description: Replay-cost characterization observation from cortex_hippo_handoff_FULL_seed_17 (single-seed): ARM_FULL_HANDOFF wall=4350s vs ARM_NO_REPLAY wall=4.47s = 973x ratio at N_replay=50 cycles, M=200 items, N_c=8192. DIRECT_CORTEX wall=3757s (same write-count, no hippo intermediate) ~ 0.86x of FULL. Implication: NREM consolidation IS compute-bound by replay cycles, dominantly Hebbian outer-product writes. Per-write cost: 4350s / (M * N_replay) = 4350 / 10000 = 0.435 ms per write at N_c=8192 (numpy CPU, float64). Cost-model: wall_replay ~ M * N_replay * O(N_c) per-write. Capacity-warn corollary: bumping M->8192 (chain-grade alpha=0.05 Hopfield) raises wall ~40x = ~50h per seed; infeasible on local_cpu without GPU/torch.cuda or matmul-batching. name: META RULE: 2x-drill capability closure when drill 1 HRR-recency-associative-recall HF AND drill 2 v2 symbolic-salience-over-substrate-features HF imply substrate state at narrative position P does NOT carry enough coref signal for symbolic cortex-layer aggregation; the capability requires richer cortex with surface-form access (M3 architecture decision)
description: Methodology rule extracted from Q2 coreference capability closure 2026-06-28. PATTERN: when capability X has TWO mechanism-class-orthogonal drills both HARD_FAIL on substrate-only-at-inference (drill 1 = associative-recall via substrate cosine matching; drill 2 = symbolic argmax over features that are themselves substrate cosine queries), the honest inference is that substrate state at the relevant POSITION does NOT carry enough signal for symbolic cortex-layer aggregation. The capability needs a RICHER CORTEX LAYER with access beyond substrate cosine queries — specifically: surface-form access (token identities, narrative structural tags, lexical co-occurrence statistics). RULE: capability_class_X-closure-2x-drill is REQUIRED before declaring capability X needs the cortex layer above substrate. One drill HF is suggestive but vulnerable to mechanism-implementation-bug. TWO orthogonal drills HF closes the box. APPLICATION: Q2 coref (this case) is the canonical first application of the closure pattern. Other expected applications: temporal-ordering-without-surface-clues, multi-step arithmetic-via-substrate-only, semantic-entailment-without-LM-prior. Each capability that needs M3 cortex-layer routing should be CLOSED via 2x-drill before routing is locked in. RATIONALE: keeps the M3 architecture decision falsifiable. If the closed capability turns out to be substrate-implementable under a third mechanism class (e.g. a deep substrate primitive we haven't tested), the closure can be RE-OPENED. CERT-neutral METHODOLOGY rule; discipline atomization per Skunkworks META atomization convention. COMPOSES WITH: 2x-drill-negative-USER discipline; M3-cortex-layer USER decision; substrate-doesn't-know-anything USER lock.

name: META_RULE: env-var-contract-must-survive-runner-dispatch -- new diagnosis category 'dispatch_infrastructure_failure' under test-design-failure rule
description: METHODOLOGY RULE (CERT-neutral): Cells with env-var-gated dispensation gates (e.g. Fix #24 GPU mandate with HDLAB_QUEUE=local_cpu_queue override) require their env-var contract to survive the runner dispatch. When the runner does not export the required env vars, the cell refuses at the gate (cell-author intent honored as designed) -- but downstream parties may misclassify this as a substrate hypothesis HARD_FAIL. DIAGNOSIS CATEGORY (new; added to test-design-failure-and-hardening rule USER 2026-06-28): dispatch_infrastructure_failure -- distinguishable from substrate negatives by: (a) elapsed_s near zero (~0.01s) -- cell never reached sweep code; (b) _phase tag stops at infra gate (e.g. gpu_mandate_check), not at sweep/aggregation; (c) all seeds produce IDENTICAL refusal verdict_msg with no per-seed variance; (d) cardinality fields are missing or zero (no phase points recorded); (e) verdict_msg references specific env-var-contract gate (e.g. 'GPU_MANDATE_BREACH', 'HDLAB_QUEUE='', 'Refusing'). PROPOSED HARDENING: (1) cell-author HEADER comment marker PRESERVE_ENV_VARS: <NAME>=<value> (greppable for pre-dispatch + post-hoc audit); (2) skunkworks SCHEMA-VET pre-dispatch gate verifies runner contract matches cell-source env-var-gated dispensation regex `os.environ.get\(['\"](HDLAB_|HDI_)`; if mismatch, SCHEMA-VET auto-fails dispatch; (3) runner-level (orchestrator) automated header extraction + env-var propagation, future. TRIGGER: pattern_completion_corruption_cliff_v2p2_dense_cliff_grid landed 3 seeds x HARD_FAIL (verdict_msg=GPU_MANDATE_BREACH; elapsed=0.01s; _phase=gpu_mandate_check) on 2026-06-28; skunkworks landed-VET caught the dispatch-infra pattern and avoided misclassifying as substrate hypothesis HF. The cell's pre-reg explicitly noted the HDLAB_QUEUE=local_cpu_queue contract at lines 129-137 of preregs/2026-06-28_substrate_pattern_completion_corruption_cliff_v2p2_dense_cliff_grid.md but the runner dispatch did not export it. v2.1 MEASURED_MECHANISM atom stands; v2.3 re-dispatch recommended with runner-side HDLAB_QUEUE=local_cpu_queue export. DOWNSTREAM IMPACT: ~3 cell-author hours of work + 3 dispatch slots wasted (all 3 seeds refused at 0.01s; tractable but wasteful); skunkworks audit time +30min to diagnose root cause; promotion path to chain-grade for pattern_completion delayed by ~1 dispatch cycle. The rule itself is the single biggest mitigation -- making the cell-runner env-var contract explicit + greppable.

name: META_RULE_AF amendment: for FULL vs DIRECT vs NO_REPLAY arm-triples, bit-exact FULL == DIRECT is FATAL (no handoff demonstrated)
description: Amendment to META_RULE_AF (arms-must-differ): when cell pre-registers FULL vs DIRECT vs NO_REPLAY arm triples (transfer / handoff / replay-effect characterization cells), the auditor MUST check FULL == DIRECT bit-exact equality in addition to FULL == NO_REPLAY. Bit-exact FULL == DIRECT means the intermediate path (hippocampus / scratchpad / intermediate codebook) was NOT exercised; the cell does NOT demonstrate the handoff. This is FATAL (HARD_FAIL) even if the verdict-heuristic ratio_FULL_to_DIRECT == 1.0 is interpreted by the cell-author as 'PASS = transfer worked' -- ratio of 1.0 means the intermediate had no effect, NOT that the transfer succeeded. EXAMPLE TRIGGER: cortex_hippo_handoff_chain_grade_M_8192_GPU_v1 (3 seeds 2026-06-28). All 3 seeds showed ARM_FULL_HANDOFF.recall_cortex == ARM_DIRECT_CORTEX.recall_cortex bit-exact (0.308837890625 / 0.3272705078125 / 0.3233642578125). cortex_norm also bit-exact. Cell-author MIDDLE_BAND verdict was rationalized as 'transfer partial'; skunkworks over-ruled to HARD_FAIL per META_RULE_AF + this amendment. AUDITOR-CHECK ALGORITHM:   (1) Identify FULL / DIRECT / NO_REPLAY (or equivalent) arms in per_seed.arms[].   (2) For numeric outcome metric M: if abs(M_FULL - M_DIRECT) < 1e-9 -> HARD_FAIL.   (3) Additionally check secondary metrics (norms, intermediate-state magnitudes);       bit-exact match on >= 2 metrics confirms intermediate is no-op.   (4) Override cell-author verdict if any of (2)/(3) trigger; rule HARD_FAIL with       cert_class = mechanism_test_design_failure.

name: META rule: bug-fix promotion requires INDEPENDENT contrastive audit; cell-owned selftests are necessary but not sufficient evidence.
description: When a cell ships a 'bug fix' that supersedes a prior HARD_FAIL atom (e.g., v2 ships fixing v1 META_RULE_AF bit-exact-arm-collapse), the cert-auditor MUST run an INDEPENDENT contrastive reconstruction -- separate from the cell's own selftests -- to verify the bug is genuinely fixed (not merely re-rationalized in a different way). The contrast should: (a) reproduce the v1 bug from scratch using the documented broken code path; (b) build the v2 fixed path from scratch and show diff_frob > 0 from the v1 result; (c) probe the load-bearing variable of the fix (e.g., zero out W_hippo before replay and show that v2 W_cortex changes -- proves the variable is genuinely in the dataflow, not just touching memory). Cell selftests can be fooled by the same author-bias that introduced the original bug; an independent reconstruction by a separate role with separate RNG/dims is the strongest evidence. PRECEDENT: 2026-06-28 cortex_hippo_handoff v2 audit, where Skunkworks built a contrast at M=256/Nh=256/Nc=512/n_replay=5 (different dims than cell smoke/full) and confirmed: v2_FULL_vs_v2_DIRECT diff=0.49, v1_BROKEN_vs_v2_DIRECT diff=0.0 (replicates bug -> contrast is correct), v2_FULL_vs_FULL_Wh_zeroed diff=0.82 (W_hippo is load-bearing). The cell's own selftests _selftest_full_arm_uses_hippo_readout + _selftest_full_arm_differs_from_direct PASS as well -- and the convergence of three independent lines of evidence (cell selftests, smoke metrics, Skunkworks contrast) is what permits the smoke-VET HARD_PASS ruling. This META rule is CERT-neutral (discipline atomization).

metadata.rule_text: When a cell-author ships a bug fix that supersedes a prior HARD_FAIL atom, the cert auditor MUST run an independent contrastive reconstruction -- separate from cell-owned selftests -- that: (a) reproduces the v1 bug, (b) shows v2 differs from v1, (c) probes the load-bearing variable of the fix. Cell selftests are necessary but not sufficient; they share author-bias with the original mistake.

name: META rule: Director spawn-prompts must report only on landings present on disk, not speculate about pending landings as if they had landed.
description: When the Director spawns a cert-auditor for a 'landed-VET' task, the spawn prompt must accurately reflect on-disk state: which seeds have metrics.json present, which are pending, which have crashed. Speculating that 'seed_13 + seed_19 may be running or pending' when no evidence exists either way wastes auditor cycles and creates phantom-multi-seed framings that lead to over-claiming. PRECEDENT: 2026-06-28 cortex_hippo_handoff v2 spawn-prompt framed as 'seed_7 HARD_PASS (seed_13 + 19 in flight)' but reality was: only smoke seed_7 had landed (M=512 not M=8192 chain-grade), backend=torch.cpu (GPU not exercised), and seeds 13/19 had NEVER been dispatched (no FULL queue entries; no output dirs). The auditor's correct action is to file SMOKE-VET HP and tell Director the cell is cleared for FULL dispatch -- NOT to atomize a chain-grade CERT increment based on a single-seed smoke. Composes with Fix #28 (verify-per-arm-metrics-before-cross-cell-claims), Fix #21 (poll filesystem for landings), and feedback_metrics_path_disambiguation_selftest_smoke_full (cite ABSOLUTE PATH for selftest/smoke/full siblings; spawn-prompts naming only anchor are MALFORMED). RULE: Director's spawn-prompt for landed-VET tasks must include the exact metrics.json paths that exist on disk, run_mode of each (smoke/selftest/full), and explicit acknowledgment of which seeds are NOT-LANDED. CERT-neutral discipline atomization.
